chunks: What the Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me of: from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from Aḥmad ibn Hilāl, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Zurārah, from one of the two of them, peace be upon them, who said:
When the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, performed wudu (ablution), whatever fell from his wudu (ablution) would be taken, and they would perform wudu (ablution) with it.

key_terms.النَّبِيُّ: the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

ai.seo_question: Can water remaining from the Prophet’s wudu (ablution) be used by others for purification?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that when the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم performed wudu (ablution), the water that dripped from him was collected and used by others for wudu (ablution). It highlights the special status of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and is cited in discussions of taharah (ritual purity) and the rulings of water.
